hook.line: Sixty-four black and white stones pack an 8×8 board. Lift two, and the jumping battle begins.
hook.say: Aloha! Let me show you the story of kōnane.

ch.say: It was born on the islands of Hawaiʻi.
p: Kōnane is a strategy game of the Native Hawaiians. It was played on a papamū — a flat lava rock carved with rows of shallow pits — with pebbles of white coral and black lava. Even the Kumulipo, the chant of creation, names it.
Captain Cook’s crew recorded it on their visits in 1778–79, and a stone board still lies at Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau on Hawaiʻi Island.

ch.say: Not the most captures — the last jump wins!
ch.cap: The 8×8 board: the two centre stones lifted, Black jumping from d6 to d4
p: Jump an adjacent enemy stone up, down or sideways into the empty square beyond, and capture it. You may keep jumping in the same direction and stop wherever you like.
If you have no jump on your turn, you lose. So the key is to cut your opponent’s jumps and keep some of your own.
